kurz: How requirement, entitlements, assets and savings contribution are calculated on a consistent basis, in which order to save, and what plans for 30-, 45- and 55-year-olds look like.

bloecke.md:
A retirement plan is an equation with four quantities: requirement in retirement, entitlements already acquired, existing assets and the savings contribution still required. Whether the end result is a portfolio, a policy or a basic pension (Basisrente) contract is only the second question. If you reverse the order, you may have a product, but you still do not know whether it is enough.

The equation fits on one page. However, it only holds if all four quantities are expressed in the same unit, that is, in the same purchasing power, at the same point in time and net rather than gross. Most private rough calculations fail on this condition. If a gross pension is deducted from a net requirement, or a gap calculated in today's euros is closed with a nominal return, the result comes out systematically too favourable, and by an order of magnitude that corresponds to decades of saving.

bloecke.titel: Calculating in real or nominal terms
bloecke.md: Either everything is calculated in real terms (today's purchasing power, real return, savings contribution increased annually by inflation) or everything in nominal terms (requirement compounded forward, nominal return, fixed savings contribution). Mixing the two is the most common and most expensive mistake in retirement provision. This lesson calculates in real terms throughout.

## Taking stock (step 1)

Before any estimate, the documents are gathered. Almost every entitlement in Germany is reported annually without being requested. The difficulty therefore lies less in obtaining them than in the fact that the documents are kept in different places and use different units. The statutory pension is shown as a gross amount without future adjustments, the company pension as an entitlement at the final age, the unit-linked insurance policy as a guaranteed annuity conversion factor (Rentenfaktor) per €10,000 of balance and the portfolio as a capital balance.

Two things are always missing from the documents. The first is the [[Pension account clarification (Kontenklärung)|pension account clarification (Kontenklärung)]]. Periods of schooling, training, child-raising and caring are often not fully recorded in the insurance account. If periods of vocational training, child-raising or caring are missing from the account, the corresponding earnings points (Entgeltpunkte) will be missing later. Since 2009, periods of schooling and university study no longer earn any earnings points themselves, but they still count as credited periods (Anrechnungszeiten), for example for the 35-year qualifying period (Wartezeit). The account should therefore be clarified thoroughly once, by your mid-forties at the latest, while evidence can still be obtained. The second is owner-occupied property. It pays no pension, but saves the basic rent. This saved rent belongs on the credit side, less the maintenance reserve (Instandhaltungsrücklage) and any residual debt still outstanding at the start of the pension.

bloecke.md:
## Converting to net (step 2)

The individual entitlements are taxed differently and bear different social security contributions. A sum of the gross amounts therefore says little. For compulsorily insured pensioners, around 12.35% is deducted from the statutory pension for health and long-term care insurance (7.3% plus half of the average additional contribution of 2.9% plus 3.6% for long-term care). The full health insurance contribution is deducted from the company pension, because the pensioner bears it alone. Private pensions in the third layer, by contrast, are almost tax-free and completely free of contributions.

The differences are large enough to reverse product decisions. For example, €300 of company pension and €300 of private pension result in two clearly different amounts in the plan.

bloecke.md:
The first misconception concerns exemption from contributions. It depends on insurance status and not on the product. Only those compulsorily insured in the health insurance for pensioners (Krankenversicherung der Rentner) pay no contributions on private pensions, Riester and capital income. For this, you must have had statutory insurance for nine tenths of the second half of your working life (Section 5(1) no. 11 SGB V, Social Code Book V, health insurance). Pensioners who do not meet this requirement are voluntarily insured. Then the company pension without an allowance, rents and capital income are subject to contributions, which can cost a three-figure sum every month.

The second misconception is double-counting the tax advantage and the payout. The state allowance that flows into the contract today is later contained in the pension, which is taxed in full. A calculation that books both as an advantage counts the same euro twice.

## From the gap to the target capital (step 3)

Requirement minus entitlements gives the monthly gap, net and in today's euros. To calculate a target capital from it, you need a capital multiple. It states how much wealth one euro of monthly withdrawal ties up, and it is the reciprocal of the assumed withdrawal percentage, multiplied by twelve. Which percentage is realistic cannot be set freely in the planning; it depends on the withdrawal strategy and the remaining life expectancy. Sound calculations use values between 3% and 4%.

bloecke.titel: Capital multiple and wealth per euro of monthly withdrawal

bloecke.md:
In 2026, one earnings point costs 18.6% of the average earnings of €51,944 as a voluntary contribution, that is, €9,661.58. Since 1 July 2026, it has yielded €42.52 of monthly pension for life. For the same €42.52 from a portfolio, around €14,584 of capital is needed at a withdrawal rate of 3.5%. Arithmetically, the earnings point is therefore about a third cheaper. In return, you give up inheritability and availability. The pension is adjusted in line with wages and not with inflation. This is more of an advantage, because wages usually rise faster than prices in the long run; in individual years, however, the adjustment can lag behind inflation.

Only two groups can make use of this: voluntarily insured persons who are not subject to compulsory insurance (Section 7 SGB VI), and compulsorily insured persons aged 50 and over who use Section 187a SGB VI to offset the reductions for an early pension. The contributions are deductible as special expenses (Sonderausgaben) within the maximum amount for basic retirement provision.

bloecke.formel:
Savings contribution = (gap × F − V × (1 + r)^n) ÷ S

F = 12 ÷ withdrawal percentage
S = ((1 + r/12)^(12n) − 1) ÷ (r/12)
bloecke.erklaerung: The first term is the target capital, the second the amount to which today's assets grow by the start of the pension without further contributions. Only the difference has to be saved.

bloecke.beispiel: Aged 45, 22 years until 67, gap €1,100, F = 343, V = €95,000, r = 3% real. The target capital is €377,300. The existing assets grow to 95,000 × 1.03^22 = €182,000. This leaves €195,300, which with the savings factor S = 373 gives a savings contribution of €523 a month. It is calculated in real terms and is increased annually by inflation.

bloecke.md:
## Order of savings goals (step 4)

This fixes the savings contribution as a figure. Where it goes depends first on what can destroy the plan, and only then on the expected return. An emergency fund prevents a car repair from forcing you to sell securities after a price slump. Occupational disability insurance (Berufsunfähigkeitsversicherung) protects the earned income from which the entire savings contribution comes. Around one in four people becomes occupationally disabled at least once during their working life, and the most common cause, at 32.34%, is mental illness. Only after that does return come into play, starting with contracts into which someone else also pays.

bloecke.unter: The order ranks risks and not products. First, whatever can destroy the plan is secured; then comes whatever accelerates wealth building.

bloecke.md: A subsidy of 15% on the amount converted is an immediate return that no asset class offers. However, this only applies up to 4% of the contribution assessment ceiling (Beitragsbemessungsgrenze), that is, up to €338 a month in 2026. Above that, the conversion remains tax-free up to €676, but is subject to social security contributions, and the subsidy lapses because the employer no longer saves any contributions. For small incomes, there is a second argument. Of lifelong pensions from additional retirement provision, for example from Riester, Rürup, occupational pensions or private pension insurance, €100 a month plus 30% of the amount above that remains exempt from offsetting in basic income support, up to a maximum of €281.50 (Section 82(4) SGB XII, Social Code Book XII, social assistance). Unrestricted portfolio assets, by contrast, are taken into account as assets.

## Three model plans (step 5)

The three model households each assume a pension start at 67, a real return of 3% and a capital multiple of 343. The requirement is estimated at around 80% of today's expenses, because savings contributions, work-related costs and, as a rule, the loan instalment fall away. Expenses for health and housing, by contrast, remain.

bloecke.md:
The example of the 55-year-old shows the problem of planning late. His gap is the smallest of the three, but his savings contribution of €795 is the largest, because he lacks the years in which the capital grows through compound interest. If this amount cannot be raised, three options remain, of which the third is the worst.

The first is to retire later. Each additional working year has a threefold effect: one year less of withdrawals, one more year of contributions and earnings points, and an avoided early retirement reduction of 3.6% that would otherwise remain for life. The second is to reduce the requirement, most effectively through housing costs, which are the largest and least changeable item in retirement. The third is to take more risk. With twelve years to go, the result can then no longer be planned reliably, because after a price slump there is not enough time for a recovery.

## Regular review

A plan that is calculated once and then filed away is out of date after five years. The method remains valid, but the inputs change, such as salary, children, pension value and tax law. How often a quantity is reviewed should therefore depend on how quickly it changes, and not on the calendar.

schritte.text: File the annual pension statement and the annual statements and update the total of entitlements. Raise the savings contribution by the inflation rate, because otherwise the real calculation turns into a nominal one without anyone noticing.

schritte.titel: Every three to five years, one evening
schritte.text: Re-estimate the requirement, check the capital multiple and the return assumption, and recalculate the gap and the savings contribution from scratch. From 55, the detailed pension report is added.
Pension account clarification with the pension insurance, so that periods of training, child-raising and caring are fully recorded in the account.

Change of job (take the company pension with you or transfer it, Section 4 BetrAVG; salary sacrifice vests immediately), self-employment, marriage, birth, divorce with pension rights adjustment (Versorgungsausgleich), a larger inheritance.

bloecke.md:
- Gross and net are confused. The standard pension of €1,913.40 is a model value for 45 average years and a gross amount. Considerably less remains after contributions and tax.
- The savings contribution is never increased. At 2% inflation, a contribution of €378 has the purchasing power of only €182 after 37 years. In a real calculation, the contribution must therefore rise in nominal terms, in the example to around €786 in the last year.
- The property is valued too highly. The saved basic rent counts, but less maintenance and residual debt. Long-term care costs cannot be paid from an owner-occupied house.
- A Riester contract is surrendered in the reform year. On surrender, all state allowances and tax advantages are reclaimed. Making the contract paid-up, or switching to the new system without losing the subsidies, which is possible from 2027, is almost always better.
- The partner is forgotten. Two separate plans do not yet make a household plan. Survivor's pension, pension rights adjustment and the question of who lives on what after the first death belong in the same plan.

The plan assumes a steady return. However, success depends more on the order of returns in the first years of retirement than on their average. A single figure in the plan cannot capture this; a simulation is needed for that.

It also assumes current law. The capital multiple depends on tax rates, the conversion to net on contribution rates and the statutory pension on floors (Haltelinien) that apply until 2031 under current law. The 2025 pension insurance report (Rentenversicherungsbericht) projects a contribution rate of 21.2% and a safeguard level of 46.3% for 2039. The recommendations of the pension commission (Alterssicherungskommission) of June 2026, including a funded additional contribution of 2%, have not yet become law. For planning, this means estimating the statutory pension cautiously and not building the plan on a political assumption.

mitnehmen: Requirement, entitlements, assets and savings contribution must all be stated net and in the same purchasing power, that is, either in real terms throughout or in nominal terms throughout.
Gross entitlements cannot be compared directly, because €300 of company pension and €300 of private pension in the third layer differ considerably after tax and contributions.
The target capital is the gap multiplied by the capital multiple, and at a withdrawal rate of 3.5%, every euro of monthly pension ties up around €343 of wealth.
Every additional euro is allocated according to risk, in this order: emergency fund, expensive debt, earning capacity, employer subsidy, subsidised layer, unrestricted portfolio.
Starting twenty years later triples the required savings contribution, and if you start late, retiring later and lower housing costs have a stronger effect than a higher equity allocation.

begriffe.text: Wealth tied up by one euro of monthly withdrawal. The multiple is twelve divided by the assumed withdrawal percentage and, at 3.5%, amounts to around €343 per euro of monthly pension.
Share of the estimated net requirement in retirement that is already covered by entitlements acquired. The remainder is the gap from which the target capital is derived.
Review and completion of the insurance account with the Deutsche Rentenversicherung so that periods of training, child-raising and caring are fully recorded.

Annual statement from the DRV under Section 109 SGB VI, sent from the age of 27 once five years of contributions have been paid. From 55, the more detailed pension report (Rentenauskunft) follows every three years.

Income comparable to a pension within the meaning of Section 229 SGB V, for example a company pension, a pension from a professional pension scheme (Versorgungswerk) or a civil servant's pension. As a rule, the full health insurance contribution is payable on it, which the pensioner bears alone; for company pensions, an allowance of €197.75 a month applies to compulsorily insured persons in 2026. Lump-sum payments are notionally spread over 120 months and subject to contributions for ten years.
